Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class SinglesColumnChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.SinglesColumnChecks
public final class SinglesColumnChecks extends Object
Singles support and gravity in a live level that does not touch loader-native automation directly: grounding at the bottom of a column, a cell resting on the one below it, visual columns lining up across differently rotated blocks, and extraction shifting a column down while carrying each item's rotation with it. Capability/Transfer-API-facing tests stay in each loader's own SinglesColumnGameTests.

  • Method Details

    • middleRemovalPreservesAndPublishesBothSurvivingColumns

      public static void middleRemovalPreservesAndPublishesBothSurvivingColumns(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: build three occupied Singles blocks, rotate the upper block and some of its items, and put comparators beside the ends. Break the middle block. Only its local contents drop; upper items keep their positions and rotations, and both surviving runs update fill and light. The fixture drains placement ticks, then inserts an upper glowstone in the same tick as removal to test pending publication at the new upper base without invoking gravity.

    • standaloneBottomIsGroundedAndFloatingCellIsRejected

      public static void standaloneBottomIsGroundedAndFloatingCellIsRejected(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: select Singles, V-place a stick on a floor, then V-deposit into an unsupported second-layer cell in another visual column. The bottom cell accepts one stick; the unsupported cell refuses it and leaves the hand unchanged.

    • upperCellUsesTheCellImmediatelyBelow

      public static void upperCellUsesTheCellImmediatelyBelow(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: V-deposit a stick into a bottom-layer Singles cell, then paper directly above it in the same visual column. Both deposits succeed; the paper rests on the stick.

    • differentlyRotatedBlocksShareVisualSeamColumns

      public static void differentlyRotatedBlocksShareVisualSeamColumns(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture uses lower and upper block rotations of one and three quarter-turns and directly fills the lower top cell in visual column 6.

      To check manually: build a Singles column to the top layer, place a Singles block above it, and Shift-right-click each block with a redstone torch to give them different rotations. Deposit into an empty upper bottom cell directly above an occupied lower top cell. Support follows the visible column.

    • extractionShiftsOneColumnAndCarriesItemRotation

      public static void extractionShiftsOneColumnAndCarriesItemRotation(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: stack a stick, paper, and apple in three consecutive cells of one Singles column. Shift-right-click paper once and apple three times with a soul torch. Release Shift and plain-right-click the bottom stick with an empty hand. Paper and apple each fall one layer with their item rotations unchanged; the vacated top cell is empty.

    • shiftKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept

      public static void shiftKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Synthetic admission fixture: an apple supports a directly seeded item currently accepted by Bar and refused by Singles. Extracting the lower item must conserve the refused item, counted in storage plus nearby drops; the test does not change policy.

      To check a tag change manually, deposit a stick above an apple in Singles, then enable a data pack adding minecraft:stick to the somestacks:ingots item tag and run /reload. Extract the apple; the stored stick is conserved despite being refused for new Singles deposits. Disable the data pack and /reload afterward.

    • drawDownKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept

      public static void drawDownKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Synthetic admission fixture: the lower block holds an apple and the upper block has a directly seeded bottom item currently refused by Singles. Extraction exercises cross-block draw-down; it asserts conservation across both inventories and nearby drops, without changing policy.

      For a visible tag-change check, build a supported column spanning two Singles blocks with a stick above the seam, then enable a data pack adding minecraft:stick to the somestacks:ingots item tag and run /reload. Extract below the seam and confirm the stick is conserved. Disable the data pack and /reload afterward.

    • extractionPreservesAnExistingGap

      public static void extractionPreservesAnExistingGap(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture directly stores a stick at the bottom and paper two layers above in visual column 2, leaving the middle cell empty. Extracting the stick shifts paper down one layer and leaves the bottom empty.

      This unsupported starting layout requires a fixture or /data merge block rather than ordinary deposits. Create a Singles block with /setblock, then merge {Items:{Size:64,Items:[{Slot:2,id:"minecraft:stick",Count:1b},{Slot:34,id:"minecraft:paper",Count:1b}]}} into its block entity. Plain-right-click the stick; paper moves to the middle cell, preserving the gap.

    • extractionDrawsAcrossDifferentlyRotatedBlockBoundary

      public static void extractionDrawsAcrossDifferentlyRotatedBlockBoundary(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture directly seeds a lower top stick and an upper bottom paper in visual column 9, with block rotations of one and two quarter-turns and paper rotation of three quarter-turns.

      To check manually: build a supported Singles column across two differently rotated blocks, rotate the upper bottom item with a soul torch, and extract the lower top item with an empty hand. The upper item crosses the visible seam with its facing unchanged; an emptied upper block disappears.

    • depositTraceStopsAtLastEmptyBeforeOccupiedCell

      public static void depositTraceStopsAtLastEmptyBeforeOccupiedCell(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal ray-selection check: a north-to-south ray through the lowest west-side row meets an occupied cell at slot 8. The trace selects the preceding empty cell, slot 4.

      To check the visible targeting, deposit a stick at the far side of that bottom row, then aim from the north through its empty cells while V-depositing. The nearest empty cell before the occupied stick receives the item.

    • depositTraceUsesFarthestCellWhenNothingIsOccupied

      public static void depositTraceUsesFarthestCellWhenNothingIsOccupied(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal ray-selection check: a north-to-south ray through the lowest west-side row of an empty Singles block selects its farthest cell, slot 12.

      To check manually, V-place Singles against a floor while aiming through an empty bottom row from the north. The first item appears in the farthest cell along the server view ray.

    • comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn

      public static void comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture checks an empty Singles block, one occupied cell, then all 64 cells: signals are 0, 1, and 15.

      To reproduce visible readings, place an outward-facing comparator beside Singles, deposit one item, then fill all cells. Read 1 and 15; after extracting all items, the block disappears and the comparator reads 0.

    • comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock

      public static void comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal layout check: a full lower Singles block and empty contiguous upper block both report 8. The empty upper block is temporary, so the exact layout is not a stable manual setup.

      To check whole-run readings, build two contiguous partly filled Singles blocks and put an outward-facing comparator on a solid support beside each. Both report the same fill after updates.

    • comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock

      public static void comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture fills a lower Singles block beneath an empty upper block, checks signal 8, removes the upper block, and checks 15.

      To reproduce the visible capacity change, fill a lower Singles block and place one item in the supported block above. The comparator reads 8. Extract the upper item; its empty block disappears and the remaining full block reads 15.
